items.title: Live: Iran retaliates for Israeli strike on major gas field as football team returns
items.description: The Israel Defense Forces have been instructed they do not need to seek approval to kill any other senior Iranian official. Follow live.

items.title: War threatens to enter a 'dangerous new stage', plus what else you should know
items.description: The ABC's Middle East correspondent Matthew Doran is in Beirut and is providing daily updates on the Middle East war.

items.title: Australia can't know how Trump plans to end this war
items.description: Even the best minds at Treasury can't know what will happen with global oil supplies, or how Donald Trump plans to end this war, with or without the help of allies.

items.title: War drone listings removed from retail platform following ABC investigation
items.description: One-way attack drones described as "cruise missiles" were listed on the popular online retail platform Alibaba for less than $50,000, the ABC has found.

items.title: Australia Zoo, government silent in search for captured totemic crocodile
items.description: Missing: One 80-year-old, 4.5 metre totemic crocodile. Last known whereabouts: Australia Zoo. Welcome to the fight for Old Faithful.

items.title: Why did the RBA raise rates as households face petrol price double whammy?
items.description: This week's rate rise left ABC readers asking "how would hiking rates stop inflation caused by an unavoidable cost like petrol that's spiking due to a war on the other side of the world?"

items.title: Live: PM says panic buying fuel isn't 'safe' as national cabinet holds virtual meeting
items.description: EU President Ursula von der Leyen will visit Australia next week to meet with the prime minister as Australia inches closer to signing a free trade agreement with Europe. Follow live.

items.title: Petrol drive-offs may not be police matter, SA's top cop warns retailers
items.description: South Australian police could stop taking reports of fuel theft unless retailers install pre-paid services at pumps, the state's police chief has warned amid a surge in petrol drive-offs.

items.title: Changes to home loans could make them cheaper and more predictable, report finds
items.description: A new report says Australian borrowers would benefit from 30-year fixed-rate home loans, and they should be made available.

items.title: Live: Market sell off on the ASX as price of oil surges
items.description: The ASX slumps at the open, while oil prices continue to make strong gains. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: 'Dire' fortunes of network behind now-defunct Kyle and Jackie O Show
items.description: Even prior to this month's colossal blow-up of the Kyle and Jackie O Show, ARN Media's future had already been teetering on the edge.

items.title: Live: Tropical cyclone Narelle intensifies off Queensland coast
items.description: Severe Tropical Cyclone Narelle has intensified into a category four system, due to make landfall tomorrow. Follow live

items.title: Could a fracture in conservative politics cost right-wing parties a seat in SA parliament?
items.description: Labor's popularity in South Australia is set to lead to a large number of seats for the party at the upcoming state election, as various right-wing parties compete for a red seat in the upper house, writes ABC Chief Elections and Data Analyst Casey Briggs.

items.title: Koala habitat logged by farmers unaware of new environment laws
items.description: Koala habitat has been bulldozed in an apparent breach of new environment laws that took effect in December, with fears farmers are unaware of their new obligations.

items.title: 'You had to fight tooth and nail': Women reveal abuse in kava gatherings
items.description: Women in Tongan communities speak out against sexual harassment at social events known as "kava gatherings", where men sit in a circle while a female server pours them the drink, known for its calming effects.

items.title: Ryan Gosling is humanity's last hope in this new space epic
items.description: Project Hail Mary hits Australian cinemas this week, joining Oscar-nominated animation Arco, off-the-wall slasher Dolly and BAFTA-winning biopic I Swear.

items.title: Put your 2026 Oscars knowledge to the test with our Academy Awards quiz
items.description: Awards season might be over for another year but the memories will live on in our minds … and in the questions of this Academy Awards quiz.

items.title: Parking politics and 'crappy' bike lanes stifling a cycling boom in Sydney
items.description: Critics say more separated bike lanes are needed to close gaps and make riding safe for a wider range of people.

items.title: France probes Shein over childlike sex dolls
items.description: Shein is at the centre of a legal battle with France after investigations found childlike sex dolls were sold on its website.

items.title: The 'catch-22' protecting Robodebt bureaucrats from criminal prosecution
items.description: Damning testimony will not land former Robodebt bureaucrats inside a courtroom, because the law empowering Australia's corruption watchdog to penetrate the right to silence is built with a shield.

items.title: Perth basketballer jailed for raping woman after night out
items.description: A semi-professional Perth basketballer is jailed for raping a woman after a night out, having texted his friends after the incident to say he "shouldn't have" done it.

items.title: No evidence for psychedelics and depression despite 'hype'
items.description: Despite growing interest in psychedelics and cannabis for treating depression, evidence the treatments work is limited.

items.title: Homecoming Queen Mary set to thrill Tasmanians
items.description: Tasmanians will get a chance to say hello to their homegrown Queen Mary when the Danish royals do a meet-and-greet with the public.

items.title: Urgent call to ensure all babies are born a healthy weight
items.description: The Productivity Commission’s latest Closing the Gap data shows just four out of 19 targets are on track. Advocates call for urgent funding to address low birth weights.

items.title: 'One of the greatest': Influential former judge dies weeks shy of 101st birthday
items.description: One of Australia's greatest judges, Sir Anthony Mason, is being remembered as an "activist judge", an unlikely figure in the Gough Whitlam dismissal and for "radical" judgements that changed the nation.
